title: HE STEPPED OUT.
paragraphs:
Not onto a dock.
Not onto a plan.
Onto chaos.

The wind was screaming.
The waves were flexing their muscle under a bruised midnight sky.
And in the middle of it all—Jesus.
Let’s step into Gospel of Matthew 14.
🌊 The Moment That Split the Night

They were professional fishermen.
Men who knew water.
Men who respected storms.

Then they saw Him.
A silhouette cutting through wind and spray.
Water bending under His feet.
“Lord, if it’s You… tell me to come.”

He didn’t ask for the storm to stop.
He asked for permission to step into it.
🔥 Fire in His Chest. Water Under His Feet.
For a few breathless seconds, Peter did the impossible.

Wet skin glistening with spray.
Hair whipped by violent wind.
Eyes locked on Jesus.
Faith louder than thunder.

Not because he was bold.
Not because he was special.
And the water that once held him… swallowed him.

Not eventually.
Not after a lecture.
Some scholars interpret this passage as a lesson on faith under pressure. Others emphasize Christ’s authority over chaos. Both are true.
The greatest miracle wasn’t Peter walking on water.
It was Jesus holding onto a sinking man.
Because walking on water impresses crowds.
But saving drowning hearts reveals the Gospel.

Shame pulls at your ankles.
Fear fills your lungs.
Your confidence sinks.

And when you falter—
His hand is already extended.
On another stormy day, years later, Peter would deny Jesus three times.

Jesus stepped into deeper waters than Galilee.
He stepped into judgment.
Into wrath.
Into death itself.

So you could step out of condemnation
and onto mercy.
Not brave men walking on waves.
A merciful Christ who rescues sinking sinners.

Comfort?
Reputation?
Addiction?
Control?
That relationship you know God told you to release?
That calling you’re afraid to answer?
What’s keeping you seated when Jesus said, “Come”?

Yes, the wind will howl.
Yes, your knees may shake.

But better to sink reaching for Jesus
than stay dry without Him.
And when you cry, “Lord, save me”—
